system.name: Consumer content platform
system.description: Feed, search, notifications at global scale

assumptions.text: 1.5x peak factor from global traffic smoothing

assumptions.impact: proportional on egress, the largest cost line

assumptions.text: 85% edge offload achievable on current content mix

components.name: Application fleet
components.justification: 75,000 peak RPS at 8 ms CPU is 600 cores; 150 instances at 60% utilisation with AZ-failure headroom.

components.name: CDN
components.justification: 1.04 PB/month egress. 85% offload saves roughly $35,000/month — the single largest cost lever in this design.

components.name: Distributed cache cluster
components.justification: 67,500 reads/second cannot reach the database. At a 95% hit rate, 3,375 reads/second reach 5 replicas.

components.name: Relational primary, partitioned
components.justification: 7,500 writes/second exceeds a single primary's comfortable range for an indexed workload.

components.name: Event stream
components.justification: 7,500 events/second with 3 independent consumer groups (search indexing, analytics, notifications) requiring independent replay. 48 partitions from throughput with rebalance headroom.

components.name: Object storage
components.justification: Media storage, served through the edge.

components.name: Observability
components.justification: 99.99% is 4.4 minutes per month; diagnosis must be immediate.

rejected_components.reason: A second search technology costs 3 points and a synchronisation pipeline whose inconsistency becomes a support burden. The existing ranking requirements are met.
rejected_components.revisit_when: Ranking requirements exceed what the current store provides, or search p95 exceeds 200 ms.

rejected_components.reason: Observability and retry policy are already handled in the service framework. A mesh adds an operational surface without a measured problem.
rejected_components.revisit_when: More than 20 services with heterogeneous runtimes needing uniform policy enforcement.

options.description: Regional cells with active-passive transactional store and regional read replicas
trade_offs: Cross-region write latency for the passive regions
Cell routing adds a layer to reason about
Partition key on the transactional store is effectively permanent

options.description: One region, maximal vertical and horizontal scaling
options.reason: Cannot meet the APAC latency requirement, and a regional failure alone would consume the annual error budget for 99.99%.

options.description: Active-active writes in all three regions
options.reason: No stated requirement for cross-region write availability. Multi-master conflict resolution is a permanent tax on every future feature, and active-passive meets 99.99%.
trade_offs: Write availability during a full regional loss

availability.explanation: 53 minutes per year. Multi-region with automated failover under 60 seconds and no manual step in recovery, cell-based blast radius containment, and 4 dedicated operations engineers to exercise it.

triggers.action: Re-run partitioning analysis; evaluate splitting the hottest entity
Investigate working-set growth; resize before database load rises
Investigate cache-key configuration; offload is the largest cost lever
Scale consumers or repartition; check per-partition variance for hot keys

triggers.window: sustained over 1 day for a material user segment
triggers.action: Re-evaluate regional placement for that segment

open_questions: Is cross-region write availability a genuine requirement, or is active-passive acceptable?
What is the actual content mix, which determines whether 85% edge offload is reachable?
